Class LessonsListTestingAutomation

java.lang.Object
testingAutomation.LessonsListTestingAutomation
public class LessonsListTestingAutomation extends Object

Title: LessonsListTestingAutomation Class.

Description: Semi-automated tests for LessonsLearnedList: the persistent list of every lesson and the subsets made from it. Requirements covered: CS-2 (see all lessons, newest first), CS-4 (search title, description, and keywords, ignoring case), CS-5 (filter by category), and CS-6 (only my lessons).

The tests run against a private in-memory database seeded with three lessons, created in this order so the expected newest-first order is known:

  1. A: "H2 file lock prevents a second connection", category Database, keywords "H2, JDBC, lock", contributor arushugal
  2. B: "PreparedStatement prevents SQL injection", category Database, keywords "SQL, security, JDBC", contributor karanpatel
  3. C: "JavaFX thread rule: use Application Thread", category GUI, keywords "JavaFX, threading", contributor arushugal

Each test is one private method named after its id, whose Javadoc states the requirement, how the test exercises the code, and the condition for a Pass. Every subset test checks which lessons came back, not only how many.

How to read the output: one "Pass:" or "Failure:" line per test id, then the suite totals.

    • list01ReadAllReturnsEveryLesson

      private static void list01ReadAllReturnsEveryLesson()

      LIST-01 (CS-2, positive). readAll returns every stored lesson.

      How: LessonsLearnedList.readAll reads the seeded database.

      Pass when: the list holds three lessons with titles A, B, and C.

    • list02EmptyDatabaseGivesEmptyList

      private static void list02EmptyDatabaseGivesEmptyList()

      LIST-02 (CS-2, negative). An empty database gives an empty list, not null and not an exception, so the page can show its "no lessons yet" message.

      How: readAll is called on a second, empty in-memory database.

      Pass when: the list is not null and isEmpty returns true.

    • list11NewestFirst

      private static void list11NewestFirst()

      LIST-11 (CS-2, positive). The list is newest first.

      How: the order of the list read by readAll is compared with the seeding order. The database orders by identifier, highest first, and identifiers are given out in creation order.

      Pass when: the titles are C, B, A in that order, and each identifier is larger than the next.

    • list03SearchFindsKeyword

      private static void list03SearchFindsKeyword()

      LIST-03 (CS-4, positive). A search finds a word that appears only in the keywords.

      How: searchByText("JDBC"). "JDBC" is in the keywords of A and B and in none of the titles or descriptions, so this also shows the keywords are searched.

      Pass when: the subset is exactly A and B.

    • list04SearchForAbsentTerm

      private static void list04SearchForAbsentTerm()

      LIST-04 (CS-4, negative). A term that appears in no lesson gives an empty subset.

      How: searchByText("quantumEntanglement").

      Pass when: the subset is empty and the full list still holds three lessons, so the search did not change the list it searched.

    • list12SearchIgnoresCase

      private static void list12SearchIgnoresCase()

      LIST-12 (CS-4, positive). The search ignores case.

      How: searchByText("jdbc") and searchByText("JAVAFX"), neither of which matches the stored text letter for letter.

      Pass when: "jdbc" finds exactly A and B, and "JAVAFX" finds exactly C.

    • list13EmptySearchTerm

      private static void list13EmptySearchTerm()

      LIST-13 (CS-4, negative). An empty or blank search term matches nothing at the list level, so a search can only narrow a list. The page treats an empty box as "no search" instead; that is tested by MOD-03.

      How: searchByText(""), searchByText(" "), and searchByText(null).

      Pass when: all three subsets are empty.

    • list05FilterByCategory

      private static void list05FilterByCategory()

      LIST-05 (CS-5, positive). Filtering by category returns the lessons in it.

      How: filterByCategory("database"), in lower case, while the stored category is "Database".

      Pass when: the subset is exactly A and B.

    • list06FilterByAbsentCategory

      private static void list06FilterByAbsentCategory()

      LIST-06 (CS-5, negative). A category no lesson uses gives an empty subset.

      How: filterByCategory("Cryptography").

      Pass when: the subset is empty.

    • list09CategoriesOffered

      private static void list09CategoriesOffered()

      LIST-09 (CS-5, positive). getCategories offers each category in use once, in alphabetical order. The page fills its category filter from this list.

      How: getCategories on the seeded list, where Database is used twice.

      Pass when: the result is exactly ["Database", "GUI"].

    • list10SearchThenFilter

      private static void list10SearchThenFilter()

      LIST-10 (CS-4 and CS-5, positive). A search result can be filtered further, because every subset is itself a LessonsLearnedList.

      How: searchByText("thread") then filterByCategory("GUI"), and separately searchByText("JDBC") then filterByCategory("GUI").

      Pass when: the first chain gives exactly C and the second gives an empty subset.

    • list07MyLessons

      private static void list07MyLessons()

      LIST-07 (CS-6, positive). filterByContributor returns that user's lessons only.

      How: filterByContributor("arushugal").

      Pass when: the subset is exactly A and C.

    • list08LessonsOfUnknownUser

      private static void list08LessonsOfUnknownUser()

      LIST-08 (CS-6, negative). A user with no lessons gets an empty subset.

      How: filterByContributor("unknownuser").

      Pass when: the subset is empty.
